newsitem.title: UK: Shopaholics lack self-esteem, seek revenge.
newsitem.headline: Shopaholics lack self-esteem, seek revenge.

text.p: Shopaholics addicted to buying things they neither want nor need are often suffering from low self-esteem, unhappy sex lives or seeking revenge against their partners, according to research published on Monday.
The first major study in Britain of shopping addiction said that 45 percent of those who shop compulsively have little or no interest in sex.

Some 30 per cent of the 101 women and men interviewed in the survey admitted going shopping to take revenge on their partner. Others attempt to shop their way out of despair and dissatisfaction in the same way that other people might turn to alcohol.
"I don't really think about anything when I'm shopping -- it's just like escaping into my own peaceful and trouble-free world," one 67-year-old woman told the researchers from Oxford University.
"It's like time stands still when I'm shopping," said a 42-year-old man.
The researchers estimated that some 700,000 people in Britain are addicted to shopping, running up debts averaging 15,000 pounds ($25,000). Most are women buying clothes that are often never worn.
One woman was divorced by her husband after she bought 160 pairs of shoes on his credit card. Another had to re-mortgage her house to fund her habit.

Those who showed elements of revenge in their addictive shopping behaviour "felt undermined and patronised and that their only responsibility was for "mundane' tasks such as housekeeping and cooking."
Less than half the sample of addictive shoppers were generally happy within their relationships and 45 percent had little or no interest in sex.

Those interviewed all recognised their addictive behaviour and all "showed the same pattern of anticipation and excitement prior to and during the shopping experience, feelings of guilt and remorse afterwards and a desire to keep their behaviour and goods secret to others," the report said.
Some 21 percent felt nervous or anxious on days when they did not go shopping.
